previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for a clotted and infected right thigh arteriovenous graft with purulent drainage from a pustule. He reported localized pain for about a week but denied fever or chills. He was started on Unasyn for suspected graft infection, and blood and wound cultures were obtained, all of which showed no growth. After hemodialysis, he underwent surgical removal of the graft due to purulent drainage. He remained afebrile postoperatively with stable labs and a therapeutic vancomycin level. Given his homelessness, he was discharged to an extended care facility for ongoing wound care and IV antibiotic administration. He will continue vancomycin indefinitely post-dialysis, receive bid dressing changes, and follow up with surgery in one week. His seizure medications were adjusted to ensure dosing after dialysis, and his heart failure and other chronic conditions remained stable.

INDICATION:  ___ man with Staph aureus sepsis and multiple abscesses,
seen on thoracic spine CT on a prior study.

FINDINGS:

LUNG PARENCHYMA:  There are multiple bilateral cavitary lung lesions
predominantly in the left upper lobe, the largest measuring 23 x 2 mm (4:65),
21 x 22 mm (4:30), 12 x 12 mm (4:112), 10 x 7 mm (4:57), 8 x 7 mm (4:100), 4 x

CARDIOVASCULAR:  There is a small pericardial effusion.  There is moderate

goiter. There is a 23 x 19 mm retroclavicular left soft tissue mass which

scapular fracture and degenerative changes of the right glenohumeral joint.
There is a bone island in the right scapula.  There are no suspicious lytic or

There are multiple enlarged bilateral cystic lesions in the kidneys, most of

IMPRESSION:

1.  There are multiple,  cavitated lesions in both lungs, predominantly in the
left upper lobe, measuring up to 23 x 20 mm, likely representing septic emboli

2. Almost complete atelectasis of the right lower lobe with obliteration of at
least two of the segmental bronchi of the right lower lobe. There is moderate
amount of airway secretions.

3.  Multiple borderline enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes, which are likely
reactive in nature.

4.  Small pericardial effusion.

5.  Multiple bilateral rib fractures and a right non-healed scapular fracture.

6.  Multiple bilateral renal cysts, which might represent multicystic kidney
disease secondary to dialysis or polycystic kidney disease. Some of the cysts

7.  The gallbladder is significantly distended and filled with sludge.  There

MEDICAL HISTORY:  ___ man with sepsis, presumed line infection.
Tunneled HD catheter pulled and needs temporary HD line.  A request was made
for a temporary HD line.

CLINICIANS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___.  Dr. ___ is
the attending radiologist who was present and supervising throughout.

ANESTHESIA:  1% lidocaine used for local anesthesia.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  Consent could not be obtained as the patient was
unable to consent and medical proxy not available.  The patient needed
emergent temporary HD line placement and the fact that he has not consented
was documented in the medical records by the primary team.  When the patient
was brought to the angiography suite, he had a cervical collar and therefore
it was not possible to place an IJ line.  This was again discussed with the
primary team and decided to place a temporary femoral line.

The right groin was prepped and draped in the standard sterile fashion.  Under
local anesthesia and ultrasound guidance with hard copy images on file as well
as fluoroscopic guidance, the right common femoral vein was punctured with a

micropuncture needle under fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance.  Contrast was
administered through the needle which showed narrowing of the long segment of
the brachiocephalic vein.  Additional intravenous contrast was administered
through the needle which demonstrated no filling of the SVC.  It was then
decided that the right femoral vein should be attempted for access.

Right groin and thigh were prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.
The right femoral vein was accessed with a micropuncture needle under
fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance.  A 0.018 wire was placed through the
needle into the femoral vein with its tip terminating in the right atrium.  A
small incision was made over the needle and the needle was removed.  A 4.5
___ micropuncture sheath was then placed over the wire and the wire and
inner dilator were then removed.  A wire was then placed through this sheath
and into the right femoral vein.  A subcutaneous tunnel was created in the
right upper thigh using local lidocaine with epinephrine and blunt dissection
extending into the right femoral vein puncture site.  A 50-cm hemodialysis
catheter was then placed through the tunnel following sequential dilation of
the puncture site.  A peel-away sheath was placed into the right femoral vein
with its tip terminating at the cavoatrial junction.  The wire and sheath were
removed.  The catheter was then placed through the peel-away sheath with the
tip terminating at the right cavoatrial junction.  Both ports of the catheter
flushed and aspirated easily.  Both ports were capped.  The new tunnel site
was secured using two non-absorbable 0 silk sutures.  Sterile dressings were
applied.  The patient tolerated the procedure well without complications.

Moderate sedation was provided by administering moderate sedation with 75 mcg
of fentanyl and 0.5 mg of Versed throughout the total intraservice time of 1
hour and 35 minutes.  The patient's hemodynamic parameters were continuously
monitored during this time.

IMPRESSION:  
1.  Successful placement of tunneled right femoral vein catheter measuring 50
cm tip-to-cuff with the hemodialysis catheter tip terminating at the junction
of the IVC and the right atrium.  The line is ready for use.
2.  Occluded SVC with multiple venous collaterals.  Right internal jugular
vein occluded. Marked narrowing of a long segment of the left brachiocephalic
vein.

PROCEDURE:  CT chest with contrast.

REASON FOR EXAM:  MRSA bacteremia and cavitary lung lesions with fever spike.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT chest without IV contrast.  5-mm and 1.25 mm axial slices
were acquired with coronal and sagittal reformats.

COMPARISON:  Previous CT ___.

FINDINGS:  There are new large bilateral pleural effusions.  Multiple well-
marginated pulmonary lesions are again redemonstrated, some of which have
changed in size and degree of cavitation, for example in the left upper lobe
was 24 x 21 now measures 18 x 16 mm and in the left upper lobe was 20 mm x 22
mm, now measures 20 x 19 mm with central cavitation.  A cluster of cavitating
nodules in the right lower lobe are partially obscured by an overlying pleural
effusion (3:39).  These nodules involve all lobes with the exception of the
middle lobe.  There are no new nodules in the upper lobes, accurate assessment
of the lower lobes is not possible due to the large pleural effusions. Within
the central airways there are secretions extending from the lower trachea into
the right main stem bronchus, the central and segmental airways are widely
patent.

Borderline enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes in the upper paratracheal,
prevascular and anterior mediastinum measure up to 8 mm, unchanged.

The aorta and pulmonary artery are normal except to note atherosclerotic
calcification in the aortic arch.  The heart size is mildly enlarged,
unchanged with a small pericardial effusion, likely physiological.

Hetrogenous enlargement of the left lobe of the thyroid, which contains
central calcification and central low density is consistent with a goiter
is unchanged. A left central venous line tip is in the brachiocephalic vein.
Multiple enlarged vascular collaterals in the anterior chest wall and axilla
suggest central venous stenosis further evaluation is not possible on a non-
contrast study.

No destructive or sclerotic bone lesions, multiple bilateral healed rib
fractures and a non-healed right scapular fracture is stable.  On the limited
views of the upper abdomen,  streak artifact limits assessment, multiple renal
cysts and calcified gallstones are unchanged.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Increasing moderate to large dependent bilateral pleural effusions, which
are incompletely evaluated without intravenous contrast.
2. Multiple cavitating lung lesions of various sizes most likely septic
emboli, predominantly in the left upper lobe and right lower lobe.
3. Multiple dilated vascular structures in the anterior chest wall and axilla
could potentially reflect collaterals in setting of central venous
obstruction, but the latter cannot be assessed for in absence of intravenous
contrast.
4. Left thyroid lobe goiter, unchanged.
5.  Multiple renal cysts and calcified gallbladder stones, incompletely
evaluated.

PORTABLE CHEST 4:32 A.M. ___

HISTORY:  Pulmonary abscesses.  Rule out interval change.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

New opacification in the left lung is a combination of the cavitated abscesses
due to septic emboli, probable increase in moderate left pleural effusion and
possibility of new and extensive consolidation in the left lung.  Previous
fissural distribution of right pleural effusion is less pronounced with erect
position.  Heart size is normal.

Nasogastric tube is looped in the airway and passes only as far in the
esophagus as the upper chest.  Left central line ends in the brachiocephalic
vein.

Dr. ___ was paged to report these findings.

PORTABLE CHEST:

COMPARISON:  ___.

INDICATION:  Feeding tube placement.

FINDINGS:  The feeding tube coils in the lower thoracic esophagus.  Please
note that subsequent chest radiograph demonstrates interval repositioning of
this device, and have been dictated separately.  No short interval change in
the appearance of the chest.

PORTABLE CHEST RADIOGRAPH, ___

COMPARISON:  Study of earlier the same date.

INDICATION:  Dobbhoff tube placement.

FINDINGS:  Dobbhoff tube has been advanced, now coiling within the body of the
stomach.  Otherwise, no relevant change since recent study.

PORTABLE CHEST, ___

COMPARISON:  Study of one day earlier.

INDICATION:  Pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  Indwelling devices are unchanged in position.  Cardiac silhouette
is upper limits of normal.  Persistent vascular engorgement and bilateral
perihilar haziness, as well as layering bilateral pleural effusions and left
retrocardiac opacity.  The latter is most likely due to atelectasis based on
review of recent CT of two days earlier.
